case_name: Bhagwan Singh and Another v State of Bihar
respondent:
State of Bihar
Supreme Court of India

5 November 1997
Cr.A. No. 564 of 1988 (Cri. A. No. 119 of 1984, D/- 15 January 1987 (Pat)), Dt. 5 November 1997.
The Judgment was delivered by : G. T. Nanavati, J.
1.  The two appellants in this appeal were convicted by the trial court along with accused Bishwanath Singh for committing the offence punishable u/s. 302 read with S. 34 IPC In the appeal filed by them the High Court altered their conviction from u/s. 302 read with S. 34 IPC
2. In the appeal filed by them the High Court altered their conviction from u/s. 302 read with S. 34 IPC to one u/s. 326 read with S. 34 IPC Both the appellants were sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 7 years and accused Bishwanath Singh was awarded rigorous imprisonment for 3 years. facts: The two appellants in this appeal were convicted by the trial court along with accused Bishwanath Singh for committing the offence punishable u/s. 302 read with S. 34 IPC
In the appeal filed by them the High Court altered their conviction from u/s. 302 read with S. 34 IPC to one u/s. 326 read with S. 34 IPC
Both the courts below have held that Raj Nath Singh had given a sphere blow on the chest of Brijlal.

The reason why the High Court altered the conviction of Raj Nath Singh from that under S. 34 IPC is that according to the evidence of Dr. C.B. Tripathi who had held the post mortem examination 8 injuries on the person of the deceased were medically interfered with and the death was caused due to pus in the brain.

What is contended us by the learned counsel for the appellant is that in view of the said finding recorded by the High Court the appellant Raj Nath Singh could not be convicted u/s. 326 read with S. 34 IPC

That apart, what we find is that Dr. Rajendra Singh (P.W. 12) has clearly stated in his evidence that injury which was found on the abdomen of Brijlal was a grievous injury and on that evidence alone conviction of the appellant u/s. 326 read with S. 34 IPC is justified.
So he is ordered to surrender to custody to serve out the remaining portion of his sentence.
petitioner_arguments: What is contended us by the learned counsel for the appellant is that in view of the said finding recorded by the High Court the appellant Raj Nath Singh could not be convicted u/s. 326 read with S. 34 IPC
court_reasoning: We are of the opinion that the said finding of the High Court is not correct.

That apart, what we find is that Dr. Rajendra Singh (P.W. 12) has clearly stated in his evidence that injury which was found on the abdomen of Brijlal was a grievous injury and on that evidence alone conviction of the appellant u/s. 326 read with S. 34 IPC is justified.
holding: So he is ordered to surrender to custody to serve out the remaining portion of his sentence.
